PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Prenatal genetic testing
Gestational Age: [redacted]
Indication: Screening for trisomy 13, 18, and 21

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniotic fluid cells using chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers. Multiple informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1437

DNA was extracted from uncultured amniocytes and amplified using fluorescently labeled primers. Fragment analysis was performed on an automated genetic analyzer.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: No abnormality detected
All markers show normal biallelic patterns
Peak area ratios within normal range (1:1 to 1.5:1)

Chromosome 18: No abnormality detected
All markers show normal biallelic patterns
Peak area ratios within normal range (1:1 to 1.5:1)

Chromosome 21: No abnormality detected
All markers show normal biallelic patterns
Peak area ratios within normal range (1:1 to 1.5:1)

CONCLUSION
Results are consistent with a normal chromosome complement for chromosomes 13, 18 and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) detected.

LIMITATIONS
- This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
- Segmental imbalances, balanced rearrangements, and other chromosomal abnormalities are not detected by this method
- Maternal cell contamination has been excluded
- This test does not screen for open neural tube defects or other structural abnormalities

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required on this sample based on these results. The referring clinician should be aware of the test limitations described above.

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD
Clinical Scientist
[redacted date]
